items.title: The SRF strategies record their distinguishing decision instead of applying it
items.why: My `all 13 ported` claim was wrong. `reflective` counts and logs merge-vs-mutate then calls the plain `epoch_step`, so the branch cannot reach the proposal. `reflective_sampler` stores `last_reflection` and never feeds a prompt, while its docstring says the sampling prompt carries prior rejections. `adaptive_meta` logs the meta decision and runs the default step. `research_then_optimize` stores `research_note` and never consumes it — `grep` finds only the two lines that set and log it. 6 of 14 strategies produce byte-identical leaderboards to `default`.
items.evidence: Fixed. Every strategy that only recorded its decision now publishes it through a new `ProposalContext.strategy` channel, and acts on it. `adaptive_meta` widens the batch by 2 on a stall (18 evals vs 16 in the audit rerun, so it now differs from `default` where it did not before). `reflective` builds a real merge — a candidate taking one parent's settings from the other — and falls back to a mutation when the two parents differ structurally rather than in their knobs, because a no-op merge would be refused as E-noop and lose the slot. `reflective_sampler` drops proposals that repeat an edit the run already refused; it reads `self.rejections` for the edits because `Run.rejections()` returns the summarised reasons a prompt wants. `research_then_optimize` and `staged_curriculum` publish their note and stage. Six tests were added that assert the EFFECT rather than the counter, which is exactly what the old tests missed: they asserted `loop.merges >= 1`, so a branch that changed nothing passed. Remaining and honest: with `optimizer=random` the model-facing decisions (research note, curriculum stage) reach a proposer that does not read them, so 4 strategies still produce byte-identical leaderboards on the tiny example — the channel is real and the distinguishing behaviour only shows with a model proposer.

items.title: check_package imports model-written code in the driver process
items.why: Its docstring says `A generated package is never imported here` and the code ends with `load_fresh(name)` -> `importlib.import_module`, then imports every declared ops module and constructs every mode. Only the *structural* check is sandboxed; the semantic half executes untrusted code with full access, which is the whole point of the issue.
items.evidence: Fixed. `check_package` no longer imports the package at all: the whole semantic check — package name, ops modules, every mode's construction, its score, its knobs, every validator rule — moved into `sandbox.verify_sandboxed`'s subprocess. `register` and `smoke` needed the manifest to name what was registered and which mode to run, and were loading the package to get it; both now use the new `sandbox.describe_package`, which reads it out of process. The two orphaned in-process helpers (`load_fresh`, `_check_mode`) are deleted, so there is no longer a function that loads a generated package in the driver. Proven by two new tests in test_create.py that spy on importlib.import_module for the package's module prefix and assert the driver imported nothing while check_package and describe_package ran to a clean result.

items.title: The lowering invents a command string instead of using refactory's callable_name
items.why: The issue says explicitly: do not invent a command string, `FnNode.callable_name` already exists; adopt `AgentNode.post_checks`; adopt Fork/Join. The lowering emits `command: 'python -m refactory_dsh.run <mod>:<fn>'` with `callable_name: None`, and `callable_name`/`post_checks` appear zero times in lowering.py. It runs, but through a convention of our own rather than the seam that was asked for.
items.evidence: Fixed, with a correction to the issue. `callable_name` IS a real `FnNode` field — `factory/workflow/primitives.py:159`, and `factory/workflow/parity.py` round-trips it — so the issue was right that the lowering dropped something. But DSH's spine does not model it: `packages/workflow/workflow-spine/src/types.ts` has `command`, `evaluator_type` and `evaluator_command`, and `callable_name` appears nowhere in the spine's source, which executes the command. So the issue's `do not invent a command string` would have produced a graph whose nodes never run. The lowering now emits **both**: `callable_name` so the IR stays faithful to refactory's language and its tooling can read it, and `command` because that is what the runtime we ship executes. Verified: the lowered graph carries both fields, every declared callable resolves, and the DSH equivalence suite still passes 6. `AgentNode.post_checks` and Fork/Join remain unadopted and are recorded as such rather than silently skipped.

items.title: retention='run' memory is declared but never discarded
items.why: `MemoryStore.forget_run_scoped` exists and is called nowhere. So a run-scoped namespace accumulates exactly like a project one, and the retention policy is a declaration rather than behaviour. The issue's own argument is that run vs project vs global 'is the difference between a memory that dies with the run and one that accumulates'.
items.evidence: Two gaps, both fixed. (1) `MemoryStore.forget_run_scoped` existed with a docstring saying `Called when the run ends` and nothing called it, so a run-scoped namespace accumulated like a project one — and on RESUME a re-evaluated candidate would read its own leftovers, making a resumed run differ from the one it resumed. `Loop._evaluate` now forgets in a `finally`, so a crash or a stop applies the policy too. (2) Found while fixing it: **memory did not cross to DSH at all**. The lowering dropped it and the node runner built its context without a store, so a mode declaring a cross-run prior worked in the walker and silently kept nothing on the runtime that ships — a difference between the runtimes that nothing reported, because the example declares no memory. `write_declarations` now carries the declarations beside the facts, `read_memory_declarations` reads them back, and `run.py` builds the store. Six new tests hold both properties.

items.title: A revision records the mode it came from, not the state it came from
items.why: The issue asks for provenance of `what it was edited from, at which state`. `_revision_source` hands the model the source files, but the output records only `revision_of: <mode id>`. You cannot reproduce or diff a revision against the exact state it was derived from.
items.evidence: Fixed. `_revision_source` handed the model the source *files*, which already worked, but the recorded provenance was `revision_of: <mode id>` alone. A mode is not fixed — the outer loop edits it — so that names a class which may have changed since, and the revision could not be reproduced or diffed against what it actually started from. `edit()` now resolves the source mode once, records its whole `revision_of_state` plus a `revision_of_digest` (the same `candidate_id` the loop uses, so a revision and a candidate that are the same state agree), and returns the digest to the caller. The test asserts the recorded state is a full state dict, that the digest matches the result, and that it identifies the state it was taken from.

items.title: create-v2 and design-v2 as modes in the default package
items.why: The original product had three meta-modes. We have create (a mode), edit (a mode), loop, and design (a mode) — but they are separate entry points, not a package. They belong in one default package, which may need exceptions the mode contract does not otherwise allow.
items.evidence: Done as `refactory_packages/meta_pack` with modes `create`, `edit`, `design`. The `-mode` suffix was dropped: `Package` validates mode names against `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$` and refused `create-mode`, and relaxing that rule to allow a tautological suffix would let every future name carry punctuation. Two latent bugs surfaced the moment the modes were validated as modes rather than merely run as entry points: (1) `CreateMode`'s `survey` node wrote `survey.json` without declaring it, and the executor SKIPS the write check for a node that declares no writes, so the graph had never passed V6 — the declaration is now there and a test holds it; (2) a package whose modes are unscored on purpose was indistinguishable from one whose author forgot, so `Mode.unscored_reason` makes the exception a declaration, the registry test accepts a stated reason and still refuses silence, the sandbox check does the same for created packages, and the loop still refuses an unscored mode as a search target. The package docstring states all three exceptions (unscored, library ops, needs a model).

items.title: A package of modes for frontier mathematics that packs non-Pythonic tools
items.why: Not every tool a mode needs is Python. Lean, mathlib and sympy need installation and a manifest, and the package must be able to declare and provision them. This is the test of whether a package can carry its tools.
items.observed: 34 passed (test_math_pack.py) with Lean installed; 562 passed / 7 skipped for the whole suite with Lean, 558 passed / 11 skipped without it
items.evidence: Two packages plus a shared declaration module. `lean_pack/prover` proves theorems in Lean 4 and scores what the proof checker accepted -- the check is `lean`, not a Python assertion. `sympy_pack/exact` establishes closed forms exactly with sympy. The tool requirement is declared through `refactory_dsh/toolchain.py`: checked before evaluation, and reported with what to install rather than crashing mid-run; a package needing nothing special still loads when the toolchain is absent. Documentation in refactory/docs/packing-tools.md. THE LEAN PATH IS NOW VERIFIED, which it was not when this item was first closed. Lean 4.33.1 was installed via elan and the checker ran for real: `verified: true`, `attempts: 1`, strategy `omega`, `exit_code 0`, and the `#print axioms` audit reports `[propext, Quot.sound]` with NO `sorryAx`, so the check that separates a proof from a `sorry` is reading real checker output rather than a stub's. Installing it also exposed a real bug, fixed in commit 27688ebc53: the mode scored 1.0 through the walker and 0.0 under `sandbox.smoke` on the same machine, because `run_sandboxed` rewrites HOME and elan finds its toolchains through HOME. The declaration now carries the environment a tool needs at run time (`Tool.env`, `toolchain.tool_env`), forwarded after containment and still secret-filtered; `sandbox.smoke` on the real mode now scores 1.0. MATHLIB IS NOW INSTALLED AND VERIFIED, and running it found two defects that no stub could have found: the statement used `∑ i in Finset.range n` which this Mathlib rejects (`unexpected token 'in'; expected ','` -- the form that parses is `∑ i ∈ s, f`), and `timeout_s` defaulted to 60s which abandoned the checker while it was importing mathlib, reporting a provable theorem as unproved. A third: `lean_version` came from the PATH while `lake env lean` ran the project's toolchain (4.33.1 vs 4.34.0-rc2), so `result.json` now carries `checker_version` from the project. The mathlib problem verifies: statement_ok 1, verified 1, strategy induction, 2 attempts, axiom audit [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] with no sorryAx. Tests are gated on MATHLIB_PATH and RAN here. THE OUTER LOOP RESULT: run on the real sympy problem, seed 0.0 (3 problems attempted, 0 verified) -> best 3.0 (all 3 verified) in 8 evaluations, bound epochs. The move that did it was one knob: `candidates` 1 -> 4. The loop also refused 9 kinds of invalid candidate across V2-V11 and I:fact_produced without spending budget on any of them.

items.title: Ship readiness: a person who has never seen this can install, run and extend it
items.why: Everything so far is legible to us. Shipping means a stranger can follow the docs from a clean clone, run the example, create a mode, pack a tool, and know what failed when it does.
items.observed: 24 passed (test_ship_ready.py); 9 passed (test_work_complete.py); ./install.sh exit 0; 564 passed / 12 skipped without the math tools, 569 passed / 7 skipped with them
items.evidence: Ship readiness is stated as a test, not as a judgement: refactory/tests/test_ship_ready.py reads the shipped documents, extracts every command line from their bash blocks, runs it, and checks the promised result. It checks four things -- that every `python -m refactory_dsh.X` a doc names imports; that every module's --help accepts the flags the doc shows; that the README links the architecture and the tutorials; and that every document the README's Documentation table links resolves. TWO REAL DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED. (1) `python -m refactory_dsh.sandbox --help` wrote its usage line to STDERR and exited 2, so a reader asking for help was told they had made a mistake, and the doc gate -- which reads a flag table off stdout -- saw nothing, which is why the sandbox CLI was the one command whose flags could not be checked. `usage()` is now the one string both paths print and `-h`/`--help` writes it to stdout with status 0; a bare invocation and an unknown flag still write to stderr and exit 2, because that is a separate decision already pinned by test_the_sandbox_cli_needs_an_instruction. The new test is not vacuous: the pre-fix behaviour (status 2, empty stdout) fails exactly its assertion, and both were run. (2) The README described the layout but never linked docs/architecture.md or docs/tutorials/, so the page a stranger opens first led nowhere; both READMEs now carry a Documentation table (architecture, tutorials, API, tool packing, hardening, contributing), line aligned at 172 lines each, with the pairing record re-recorded. ALSO: docs/api/reference.md is generated from the code and had drifted; the new usage() export made that visible and test_docs_api.py fails when the two disagree, so the reference is checked rather than trusted. items.title: SRF's own optimizer (lab/map_elites.py) was vendored and never ported
items.why: The objective named this gap explicitly. Thirteen SRF *modes* were ported and the count of 'SRF ports' was complete against a list that omitted the optimizer SRF keeps beside them in srf/lab/. Nothing in the repository referenced map_elites.
items.evidence: Ported as the `map_elites` strategy on the loop's own vocabulary. MAP-Elites keeps one champion per cell of a feature grid rather than one best candidate overall, so a weak candidate in an empty niche survives beside a strong one in a crowded niche and selection can return something that is not the best -- which no other strategy here does. Features: graph size, structural-vs-settings move, and step budget. NicheArchive refuses a weaker candidate in an occupied niche and accepts one in an empty one. The count is now two constants, SRF_PORT_COUNT=13 and SRF_LAB_PORT_COUNT=1, because a single total would let one be dropped as long as something else was added; the registry test asserts both and asserts `map_elites` by name. Three effect tests on the section-3 standard (weak-in-occupied-niche does not displace the champion; weak-in-empty-niche is kept; selection spans more than one niche and more than one score; the niche map reaches the proposer via ProposalContext.strategy), plus a real loop run from the CLI. Documented in refactory/docs/hardening.md section 8 and refactory/docs/architecture.md section 6.

items.title: The evaluator is not an abstraction: the loop's loss is a string and an if-branch
items.why: Two of the loop's three extension points had a base class and a registry; the third -- how a mode is run to get the score the loop learns from -- was a string compared against a literal. There was nowhere to put a third evaluator, and a third is what an interactive run needs.
items.observed: 8 passed (test_evaluators.py), incl. the DSH equivalence case; 584 passed with --run-integration
items.evidence: refactory_dsh/evaluators.py: Evaluator (name/evaluate/from_settings), WalkerEvaluator (runs in-process, owns the run-retention forget), DshEvaluator (lowers and runs on DSH), REGISTRY, names(), create() that fails loud, register(). Loop._evaluate no longer branches: it calls self.evaluator and assigns the candidate once. Both paths already returned RunResult so no result type was added, and the duplicate candidate.json writer is gone -- every candidate records its ports now, whichever evaluator ran it. Removed a validate() check that could never fire because create() raises first. Tests assert the seam, not the implementations: a third evaluator is registered and used with no edit to loop.py, and _evaluate does not branch on the name. Both verified against the code they replaced -- restoring the old hardcoded dispatch fails both, removing it passes.

items.title: science is a package of modes, not a runtime: retire --profile science
items.why: Two runners only: the walker (headless) and DSH (interactive, with the CEO layer). --profile science is a third thing from the previous system, and science is meant to name a package of modes and nothing else.
items.observed: 633 passed with --run-integration; the renamed profile boots and agrees with the walker (28 passed across test_equivalence + test_loop_as_mode)
items.evidence: RENAMED THE BUNDLE so `science` names only a package of modes, which is what it was always supposed to be: packages/bundle/science -> packages/bundle/graph, @deepseek-ai/dsh-science -> @deepseek-ai/dsh-graph, and --profile science -> --profile graph. The rename is total, not cosmetic: the package manifest, the TS path mapping in tsconfig.base.json, the project reference in tsconfig.host.json, apps/cli's dependency, the bundle's own cordis.patch.yml, the internal plugin and service ids (science-runner -> graph-runner, science-startup -> graph-startup, scienceStartup -> graphStartup, SCIENCE_STARTUP_SERVICE -> GRAPH_STARTUP_SERVICE, ScienceStartupValues -> GraphStartupValues), the three call sites (dsh_runtime.py and the two DSH test files), the persona wording, and every document that told a reader to run --profile science. Both READMEs of the bundle are rewritten and the bilingual pair re-recorded; zero mentions of 'science' remain in the bundle. A FINDING WORTH KNOWING, found by running it rather than by reading: a profile is MACHINE STATE, created by `dsh plugin --profile <name> add <package>`, not derived from the bundle name -- so ~/.dsh/profiles/science stayed behind and `--profile graph` stopped with 'profile "graph" does not exist' until the new one was added. The bundle README already documents that one-time step for whichever name is current, so the operational model is unchanged, but any machine or CI that runs a mode on DSH needs it once. HONEST LIMIT: the old ~/.dsh/profiles/science is left in place rather than removed; it is the reader's machine, and deleting a profile is a destructive step to take with them, not for us.

items.title: Steering a run while using it: user gates and the intent ledger
items.why: A person using a mode can change context but not structure; the outer loop owns structure. Today a run cannot pause and ask, and nothing records what the person said. The previous system had a User Intent Ledger and we threw it away, along with the gate that checked fidelity.
items.evidence: refactory_dsh/steering.py: Ledger (append-only, timestamped, seeded once, in the RUN directory so it travels with the run and survives resume), annotate() which folds it into EVERY AgentNode prompt of the lowered workflow, interactive() as the one entry point, and fidelity() which checks the precondition. LoopConfig gains `intent`; Loop._seed_ledger writes it; the console gains a `steer` verb (--seed / --note / --kind) and the loop CLI gains --intent. THE LAYER IS INERT WHEN UNUSED: an empty ledger renders the empty string and annotate returns the workflow it was given, so a run nobody steered is the run it would have been and the interactive and headless paths stay comparable -- proved non-vacuous by making render() return something for an empty ledger, which fails the identity assertion. THE GRAPH DOES NOT CHANGE: steering is context, applied to the IR rather than to nn.Node, so modes stay Pythonic and to_workflow knows nothing about it (asserted by inspecting its source). BUG-05 IS REFUSED RATHER THAN REPRODUCED: the previous ledger held the literal 'Build something useful.' because REFACTORY_INTENT never arrived, and the fidelity gate then checked nothing while reporting a pass; Ledger.seed now refuses that string and refuses an empty request, and fidelity() reports a missing, empty or placeholder origin. Three kinds because they are not the same act: info, correction, and constraint (which must be respected, not merely known). VERIFIED END TO END on a real run: --intent seeded the ledger, `console steer --note ... --kind constraint` appended to it mid-run, and the file shows both timestamped entries. HONEST LIMIT: the gate checks that an intent exists, not that the work matches it -- whether work is traceable to intent needs a model to read it, and that is stated in the docstring rather than implied. CORRECTION, ADDED AFTER THE FIRST CLOSE: this was closed as landed while its FIRST acceptance criterion was not done. `lowering` still hardcoded evaluator_type='fn' and nn.Node had no gate kind, so a MODE COULD NOT DECLARE A PAUSE POINT -- the mechanism the whole design rests on, since an intent ledger nobody can be asked about is a file. That is the same failure this session audits elsewhere, made while auditing. FIXED: Node.gate_kind is 'fn' | 'user' | 'agent'; fn requires an evaluator and the other two REFUSE one (a gate with two answerers has an answer that depends on the runtime); lowering emits the declared kind and a command only for fn; and a walker meeting a user gate REFUSES, naming the node, rather than inventing a verdict -- a run that pauses cannot quietly decide for the person, and an invented verdict is indistinguishable from one they gave. The answer arrives through RunContext.verdicts, which an interactive run fills and a resumed run replays. A SECOND DEFECT was found by an existing test rather than by this work: the first version of Node.to_state serialized gate_kind unconditionally, which changed EVERY mode's state dict and therefore every candidate id the loop has recorded, so a resumed run would no longer match itself and the search moved for reasons unrelated to the search -- test_no_batch_slot_is_silently_lost caught it as a vanished batch slot. A field at its default is now omitted. Six new tests, verified both ways: restoring the hardcoded fn fails the declaration test. Recorded in refactory/docs/hardening.md section 9.

items.title: D15's adopting loop was never built, so a run's winner is unreachable
items.why: D15 says create, edit, design and an adopting loop all produce something new. Three exist; the adopting loop does not. A run records what the best candidate scored, not the state that scored it.
items.observed: 9 passed (test_adoption.py); adopted sympy_pack/exact's winner reproduced 3.0 exactly, source digest unchanged
items.evidence: refactory_dsh/adopt.py: best(run) reads the winner's FULL STATE from journal.jsonl -- the only artifact that carries a state; report.json carries the score, state.json's population carries the edits, and console candidate returns a diff, so none of them can be run. adopt(run, as_name=) writes a NEW package whose mode subclasses the searched class with the winning state pinned, so the ops, the knobs and the score() are the same code and only the state differs -- which is what makes the comparison against the baseline meaningful. It refuses to overwrite an existing package and records provenance (adopted_from, run, candidate, score, edits) in .adopted.json. Console gains `best` (state opt-in via --state) and `adopt --as NAME`. VERIFIED on the real run at .factory/repro: best returns candidate 8f7ef8f4648c scoring 3.0, and `registry smoke adopted_exact/exact` scores 3.0 -- the adopted artifact reproduces the winner. Nine tests, including D15's property: adopting leaves the source package byte-identical and the run byte-identical. Non-vacuous: planting a real write into the source package fails the byte-identical test, and removing it passes.

items.title: Use the tower: nothing has ever searched loop_mode/loop's own knobs
items.why: D14 says the loop is itself a mode so a further loop can search the loop. It is expressible and unused, so the claim it was built to make has never been demonstrated.
items.observed: 21 passed + 1 skipped (test_loop_as_mode.py); tower run seed 0.875 -> best 1.04
items.evidence: D14's claim demonstrated rather than described. Ran a real outer loop over loop_mode/loop: seed 0.875 -> best 1.04 in 3 evaluations, the winning edit being `set_knob batch_size 4 -> 8`. architecture.md section 11 recorded 'expressible, not yet used' and no longer does; section 9 now carries the command and the result. The test that stood here asserted only that batch_size, epochs and optimizer are VISIBLE in the context -- expressiveness, not use -- so it was strengthened to run the search and assert the leaderboard, and a second test pins the lever deterministically on seed 0 (batch_size 4 -> inner best 0.875, 8 -> 1.04). Without the lever test a search over a surface that cannot move would still pass its own test.

items.title: A failed model call looks like a search that found nothing
items.why: A dead key, a quota, or a wrong model name all present as a run that scored nothing -- a claim about the mode rather than about the model. It is the first failure a person hits with their own key.
items.evidence: PROBED, AND THE ISSUE'S PREMISE WAS WRONG. I filed #38 from a comment in optim/base.py rather than from behaviour, guessing that a failed model call was caught and continued. Checking the call path showed Optimizer.propose_valid -- the method holding both the k-round retry loop and the except-Exception guard -- is called ONLY BY TESTS. The loop's default path is Loop.optimizer_step -> Loop.propose -> optimizer.propose, unguarded, and model.py's docstring claiming failures become 'a generation with no proposals' described a path the loop never reaches. So a failing model did not hide: it raised out of loop.run(), dying before report() and losing every evaluation already paid for. That is worse than the issue claimed, and the correction is posted on the issue. FIXED by guarding the loop's own propose path: the round is recorded in Optimizer.proposal_failures and counted in proposal_rounds, and returns no proposals rather than raising. The report now carries a proposer block (rounds, failures, failure_count, all_failed, finding) and renders a 'Did the proposer answer?' section only when something failed -- a run where every round failed says it is not a search result. Three tests: the run survives a dead client; the report names the failure and the reason; and a healthy run does not claim one, so the finding cannot become noise. model.py's docstring is corrected.

items.title: optimizers and outer loops are one bucket: all 15 strategies register as OuterLoop
items.why: outerloop.py says 'most research ideas live here [in the proposer]' and the registry disagreed: every SRF-derived name was an OuterLoop and the Optimizer registry held two hand-written entries and no port.
items.evidence: THE CAUSE WAS THE CONTRACT, NOT THE FILING, and finding it is what made the fix possible. Loop handed a proposer select_parents(elite) and Candidate.describe() carries no state, so a proposer only ever saw the elite's states: island selection, a niche grid and a tournament over an archive could not be written as proposers however they were filed. FIX: Loop.optimizer_step now hands over the evaluated population and the optimizer selects; ProposalContext gains `elite`, the count an optimizer with no parent policy should take, so widening the pool does not silently change what random and autoresearch propose. THE SPLIT: four of SRF's thirteen modes (scs, evox, openevolve, karpathy) moved to optim/policies.py as proposers, and map_elites joined them -- it was added as a 15th OuterLoop and SRF_LAB_PORT_COUNT existed to make the totals add up around that placement. Asserted rather than described: 13 - len(SRF_OPTIMIZER_PORTS) is the loop count, every optimizer port is in the optimizer registry, no name is in both buckets, and every registered name is one or the other. The CLI's --optimizer choices now come from the registry instead of a hardcoded pair, which is how five optimizers could be registered and unreachable. TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY THE NEW TESTS, not by reasoning: (1) MapElitesSelector.features read state['nodes'] where the nodes are at state['graph']['nodes'], and .get returns None rather than raising, so every candidate landed in one cell -- a niche grid that is a single bucket and looks like it works; caught by a test aiming at a known-empty niche. (2) island_of derived the island from hash(candidate.id), and Python salts string hashing per process, so the same candidate sat in a different island on a resumed run than when it was evaluated; inherited from IslandArchive and invisible until a run is resumed. It uses a digest now. Also fixed: _elite must reproduce Loop.leaderboard exactly -- score descending with id as the tie-break, unscored excluded, the population fallback -- because a subtly different ordering changed the search enough to lose a refusal a layer early (test_history caught it).

The ledger is folded into the agent prompts by steering.for_run in both runtimes, so a mid-run note reaches later agent nodes. Recorded as a run in architecture.md section 11. items.title: The fidelity gate checks the precondition, not the output
