items.title: knob_attribution.untried lists the values of a bounded numeric knob
items.why: The gradient's whole purpose is telling an optimizer that a value nobody tried is not a value that failed. It answered empty for every numeric knob, so a step knob declaring 1..4 reported nothing untried after two of four values had run, and the one improving value was invisible.
items.evidence: Found by a live run: 21 evaluations of counting_pack/fixed_step, step tried {2: 19, 3: 2}, untried [], while step=1 scores 1.0 and step=4 scores 0.25. _untried now enumerates an int knob with both bounds declared, reusing the same finite set Knob.alternatives offers a sampler; an open-ended numeric knob still answers empty. Both ways: the new test failed with `assert []` on the old code and passes on the fix, and the same run now reports untried [1, 4] and target untried [1,2,3,4,6,7,8].

items.title: The DSH path runs the candidate's knob values, not the op defaults
items.why: run_on_dsh and interactive.command json.dumps'd a value that lowering.knob_environment already returns as a JSON string, so the node runner read a string where it needs an object and every node fell back to its op's hardcoded default. The two runtimes ran different programs.
items.evidence: Evidence: counting_pack/fixed_step's seed (step=2, target=5) scored 1.0 on DSH with trace increments [1,1,1,1,1] where the walker scored 0.5 with [2,2,2]; after the fix DSH scores 0.5 with increments [2,2,2]. json.dumps(knob_environment(state)['REFACTORY_KNOBS']) produced '"{\"target\": 5, \"step\": 2}"'. Both ways: the new assertions failed seeing the double-encoded string and pass after dropping the outer dumps. test_equivalence.py never caught it because it builds its own command line instead of calling run_on_dsh; that gap is filed in the issue.

items.title: run_on_dsh hands DSH an absolute work directory
items.why: DSH refuses a relative session cwd, and the CLI's default run root is relative, so a dsh-evaluated run failed every candidate with "session header cwd must be an absolute path" and reported best_score 0.0.
items.evidence: Every candidate in the relative-root run carried exit_ok false and that error; the same state under an absolute root ran. run_on_dsh now resolves the workdir at the boundary that hands it to DSH. Both ways: the new test saw --workdir 'relative/run' before the fix and an absolute path after it.

items.title: A node in a workspace package imports in the node's own process
items.why: A package created into .factory/packages is importable only where registry.install_workspace ran, which is the driver's process. DSH runs each node as its own command, so the op could not be imported and a created mode scored nothing on the runtime that ships while scoring under the walker.
items.evidence: Reproduced by hand: the node command in the candidate's work directory failed with ResolutionError: cannot import 'refactory_packages.counting_pack.ops': No module named 'refactory_packages.counting_pack', and the spine recorded only 'start exited with code 1'. run_node now applies the same workspace root the driver uses (registry.install_workspace(project_root())), idempotently. Both ways: the new subprocess test failed with that import error and passes on the fix; the end-to-end dsh run reached both candidates and scored them.

items.title: A failed node records the stderr that says why
items.why: The spine status carried only 'run exited with code 4', so the reason a node failed was nowhere a reader of the run could see it — the same class as #38, where a failure looks like a search result.
items.evidence: The candidate's spine-status.json read {"status": "failed", "error": "start exited with code 1"} while the node's stderr (the ResolutionError naming the missing module) existed nowhere in the run directory. report() now appends the node's bounded stderr to the recorded error, keeping the exit code alone when the node said nothing. Both ways: the stderr test failed on the old code and passes after; a second test pins the empty-stderr arm, which also keeps the file at per-file 100% coverage.

items.title: adopt reads a mode that lives in the workspace
items.why: The loop runs in its own process, so the process running adopt never installed .factory/packages; _class_name read the mode with registry.load(package, None), which skips that install, so the winner of a created package's run could not be frozen at all.
items.evidence: Live: `console adopt --run counting_pack-fixed_step-20260921-194815 --as counting_tuned` returned {"error": "cannot import package 'counting_pack': No module named 'refactory_packages.counting_pack'"}. The project is threaded from adopt() into _class_name/_mode_source and registry.load now gets it. Both ways: the new test reproduces the missing module (with the workspace root dropped to stand in for the run's separate process) and passes on the fix; the live adopt then wrote counting_tuned, which scores 1.0 on the walker and 1.0 on DSH with trace increments [1,1,1,1,1].

items.title: A refused adoption leaves nothing behind
items.why: The destination and __init__.py were written before the step that can fail, so the residue could never be adopted over (adopt refuses an existing name) and every catalogue scan warned about a package whose mode module was never written. The same defect #47 fixed for registry add.
items.evidence: Live: after the failed adopt, .factory/packages/counting_tuned held only __init__.py, `console modes` printed package_unavailable for it, and the retry refused because the name existed. The write now removes the destination on failure. Both ways: the new test saw the residue on the old code and no directory on the fix.

items.title: The report names the batch the epoch bound drops, instead of changing when it is asked
items.why: The final epoch's proposals were installed, counted, and never evaluated: a live 2-epoch run kept 10 candidates that nothing ran. I first changed the semantics (--epochs N means N evaluated batches) and reverted it: the full suite showed three tests use epochs=1 because one epoch still asks, a fourth shifted with the proposal mix, and epochs=1 meaning 'sweep only' is a functional surprise. Proposing ahead is the designed pipeline; the harm was a report that could be read as if everything kept had run.
items.evidence: report.json now carries `unevaluated` (the ids installed and never run) and report.md names them in the inner-runs section. Both ways: the new test failed against the pre-accounting code with KeyError: 'unevaluated' and passes here. The behavioural attempt is in the history as e7f8d4113b and its revert as 074c28bab0, with the reasoning on the issue.

items.title: remote-factory's create-v2 and design-v2 are the default package's modes
items.why: The default package's create/edit/design were a single pass; create-v2 and design-v2 add a research director, a strategy director with intent coverage, a person's approval before anything is built, three reviews in parallel, and an overwatch pass that audits their evidence. None of it could be expressed: the vocabulary had three node kinds and no barrier or iteration.
items.observed: 25 passed (test_default_package.py); both modes lower to IR and pass the IR validator, and DSH's own validateGraph accepts them with ForkNode/JoinNode intact; a live model-driven create run completed end to end in 1479s over 23 iterations.
items.evidence: meta_pack became default_pack; the vocabulary gained fork/join/data with lowering, V12 and fork/subgraph reachability; the walker runs forks and joins to the same barrier as DSH. Live real-model runs executed the v2 phases (research director with subagents, strategy director, synthesize_strategy, design-v2's design_doc, emit, materialise, validate, the QA fork, synthesize_qa, gate_qa, overwatch, gate_overwatch, register, smoke) and refused at the person's gate rather than approving it themselves; the first full run then failed at qa_director with the 300s completion ceiling, which is why that ceiling is now 1800s and settable (f92276b0fb). Supplying the person's verdict with verdicts={'gate_strategy': 'proceed'} produced the package live_counting with smoke_score 1.0, sandboxed, qa-gate 'proceed: no blocking finding' and overwatch-gate 'proceed: overwatch passed'; re-smoked independently by hand: exit_ok true, score 1.0, and the step knob moves the score (step 1 -> 5/1.0, 4 -> 8/0.25, 7 -> 7/0.333 for target 5).

items.title: A data node iterates and a Task binding supplies and judges its items
items.why: The dataset half of the port: a mode could declare neither an iteration nor a binding, and `--data-node`/`--task` were prompt text with no path that set them and no check that they were honoured.
items.observed: 12 passed (test_items.py); test_equivalence.py's data-node case runs one data-driven mode on the walker and on DSH and compares the facts; 115 passed (workflow-spine).
items.evidence: One loader for both runtimes: refactory_dsh/items.py calls nn.executor.load_items, the function the walker calls, for inline items, a directory/jsonl/csv source and a Task's instances(), and runs the Task's setup/verify around each pass. The spine iterates a data node (DataPass, startPass/endPass, the exit completing a pass) and the plugin drives the loader's list/begin/end around each pass, so a subgraph containing agent nodes is walked one node at a time; an empty selection completes the node, and a graph with a data node and no configured loader is refused at load. validateGraph refuses a gate exit, an entry that cannot reach its exit, an unknown subgraph node and an edge into the data node's own subgraph. Fixing the loader path found a live defect (load_items used json without importing it), now covered by the JSONL test.

items.title: Asking the CEO reaches list, choose, start and read
items.why: The conversation-first half of the picker issue: a person should be able to ask in words and have the CEO use the right tool, without the tool having to fail to teach it.
items.evidence: Verified in the real GUI: one plain-language ask made the CEO call modes, list the counting modes, call start with the mode and settings, and return the run id, which finished at best 1.0. The catalogue now carries the action that runs each mode (start, or the authoring verb), the tool's description says which action to use and in what order, and start refuses an authoring mode synchronously naming the verb to use instead. The picker widget is built and uncommitted in the working tree (packages/client/ui-refactory and packages/refactory/refactory-console); its ledger item is recorded with the commit that lands it, because every `done` item must name a commit git can resolve.

items.title: The picker: a mode, strategy and package panel over the same console the tool reads
items.why: Issue #49's second half. #28's acceptance asks for "a named choice with its description, not a free-text field", and the conversation-first surface only reaches the model; the browser needed its own host path to the console.
items.observed: 146 tests passed across 9 files (tool-refactory, refactory-console, ui-refactory), including service-live.spec.ts driving the real .venv console through the real local subprocess provider; client per-file coverage 100% on all four metrics; pnpm run test:gui 4735 passed; the panel was driven in a real page: the Modes tab read 17 described modes, 10 outer loops, 8 optimizers and 2 evaluators, and Start began counting_pack-fixed_step-20260922-003904, which the status section then read (running, best score 1, 4 evaluations).
items.evidence: packages/refactory/refactory-console is a Typert Remote service (refactoryConsole) that holds the same Console the model-facing tool holds — both go through resolveConsoleSettings/startInvocation/registryInvocation in tool-refactory's new ./console entry — so a choice made in the panel is the invocation the tool makes. packages/client/ui-refactory registers kind `refactory` into ctx.sidebarRightTabs and a body into sidebar.right.pane.tab: a mode picker, three strategy pickers (name + own description), a package list with enable/disable/remove/import, start, and on-demand status with refresh and stop. Refusals carry codes (refactory/authoring-mode names the verb the catalogue's own `action` field reports). Wiring: the host row in the web-app composition (where the gateway discovers host services), the client row in the bundle, the tsconfig aggregates and the web-app dependency. Fixed while verifying: the generated lib/typert.host.js imports zod, which the package had not declared (91 web-lane files failed to boot until it did); the panel's 1px neutral borders violated the ui-theme hairline rule; and the console side-bundle needed a declared entry in the workspace publication policy. A GIF of the panel (refactory/docs/assets/refactory-picker.gif, 212 KB) is recorded from a server booted from this tree and is referenced from docs/subsystems/refactory.md; it is linked from issue #49.

items.title: One entry point (`uv run refactory`), and a run that must finish
items.why: The repository had no entry point: every act meant knowing an interpreter path and a module name, the authoring path could not answer its own person's gate from the CLI, and a run whose CEO backgrounded a subagent was reported as finished with a score of 0.
items.observed: The offline recipe set passes 15/15 in a fresh clone; `refactory ceo --mode create` completed all 23 nodes of create-v2 on DSH and produced haiku_pack/haiku (one agent node), which `refactory run haiku_pack/haiku --intent "a haiku about the ocean"` then ran to a real 5-7 haiku with syllable_accuracy 1.0.
items.evidence: A root pyproject.toml with the three local packages as editable sources makes `uv sync` the whole install and `uv run refactory …` every command (install.sh does submodules + pnpm + uv sync + the DSH profile). `cli.py` is one verb per question, dispatching onto the module that owns it; `ceo "<an idea>" --mode design|create|edit` runs the authoring mode on DSH with the terminal attached, with name/brief/check travelling as knobs and `--approve GATE=VALUE` for an unattended run. The graph profile mounts tool-subagent foreground-only and the runner reads .refactory/spine-status.json, failing with the nodes still due instead of exiting 0 on an abandoned graph. Node commands resolve the project through paths.project_for_nodes() (REFACTORY_PROJECT, set by the graph bundle), so a created package lands in the workspace rather than inside the run. tools/recipes.py is the single list of documented commands: the HTML tour renders it and check_recipes executes it. Also fixed on the way: `interactive`/`refactory run` refused to start because DSH needs an absolute session cwd.

items.title: The revision comparison lived in a function the console script never called
items.why: `refactory ceo "…" --mode edit` documents a revision that refuses a regression. A run of it showed no comparison happened at all on that path: `facts.json` recorded `revision_of` and nothing else, the package's `.origin.json` said only `origin: create-mode`, and the whole comparison — before score, after score, the source state and its digest — existed only in `edit.edit()`, which the CLI never reaches. The `edit-mode` recipe asserted `before_score`/`after_score` in the output, strings the run could not produce, at a tier no gate runs by default.
items.evidence: Fixed and verified end to end. The `smoke` node now scores the mode being revised as well, compares the two, and fails the run naming both scores; `before_score`/`after_score`/`regressed` are recorded in the run's `revision.json` and, with `revision_of` and the source's whole state plus digest, in the package's `.origin.json`. Two modes are compared only when one smoke run measures both: an unscored source, or one whose graph calls a model, is recorded as not compared with the reason, so it cannot be read as a pass. `allow_regression` is a declared knob reachable as `ceo --knob allow_regression=1`. `interactive.run` prints one line of the run's own facts when it finishes, which is what makes the recipe's promise checkable and was verified by running the documented command at the model tier (`check_recipes --tier model --only edit-mode`). A run of the new suite also exposed the guard this file records: with no `package_path` in its facts the comparison wrote `.origin.json` into the working directory. Reproduce: pytest refactory/tests/test_edit_design.py -q

items.title: A search wrote an intent ledger that no node read
items.why: `optimize --intent "…"` and `refactory steer --run <search> --note "…"` both write the run's ledger, and `console steer` reports it back — but the loop evaluates each candidate in `runs/<id>/` and the steering transform reads the ledger of the directory it is handed, so nothing in a search ever saw the intent or a mid-run note. Found by running it: with a scripted model, the candidate's prompt contained neither the ledger nor the intent.
items.evidence: Fixed by `Loop._carry_ledger`: the run's ledger is copied into each candidate directory before the evaluator runs it, so both runtimes fold it in (the walker in `execute`, DSH as the lowering transform) and the candidate directory keeps a record of what the person had said when it was evaluated. Two tests, each shown failing before the fix and passing after: the candidate's agent prompt contains the ledger and the intent, and a note appended between two evaluations reaches the second candidate and not the first. The README's read-and-steer table now says what steering does and how it arrives, tutorial 06 covers a search as well as a run, and architecture.md records why the copy exists.

items.title: A run could not choose its model, and a route that did not exist was not an error
items.why: Found by answering "how do I configure models?". Three defects in one path: the graph profile's --model/--provider were parsed and then discarded, because the model-selection middleware installed on the CLI-created agent was seeded from agentDefaultModel's settings default and rewrites every request from it; the one-shot profile had no --model at all, so `refactory optimize --model X` (documented) ran `dsh --profile headless --model X` and got `unknown option '--model'`, failing every autoresearch proposal; and an unknown provider answered from the default model instead of failing, so a run attributed to one model was produced by another. Per-run model choice is part of ship readiness (#31): without it a stranger can only change the global default.
items.evidence: Fixed in two commits. The one-shot profile gained -p/--provider and --model (parsed in the startup provider, published on the startup service, wired through the row config) and both bundles now install the selection middleware with the effective selection, so a named model is the one requests route at; an unknown provider now exits 1 with NO_ADAPTER naming the route. Refactory exposes --model/--provider on run, ceo and optimize, with the module entry points taking --provider beside the existing --model. Verified by running it, not by reading: an openai-completions route pointed at a local OpenAI-compatible server through --patch answered `dsh --profile headless --provider local-test --model test-model` with that server's text and the server logged `model=test-model`; the same was repeated through the graph profile (final text = the fake server's, server log = the named model). Reverting the middleware line makes the new headless spec assert the settings default and fail. The READMEs gained a Models section (advisory catalogue, the GUI Models page, settings.yaml and the credential store, a verified local-route example, per-run flags), and an Agent Note records why the middleware's current is the authority.

items.title: The refactory tool could not answer a user gate, so authoring from the GUI always failed
items.why: `create`, `edit` and `design` pause at `gate_strategy`, a gate a person owns. The CLI (`ceo --approve`), the console (`--verdict`) and the tool's own `steer` action all had a way to state that answer; the tool's schema did not, so every authoring action from the Web GUI was a headless run that refused the gate.
items.evidence: The tool gained `approve` (an array of `GATE=VALUE`) forwarded as repeated `--verdict` for create/edit/design, and `Console.argv` learned to emit one flag per element so a repeatable option survives the hop. The action descriptions now say the call cannot pause to ask, so the model asks the user for the plan approval first and passes it with the call. Four new specs: the verdict reaches argv for all three verbs, the failure text keeps the console's reason, the status card reports an authoring run's own progress, and the default timeout is at least 30 minutes. The GUI-facing half of the six defects is the tool's; the pipeline half is c1b9b1ded2.

items.title: A forwarded refusal lost its stderr, so an authoring failure reported exit 2 with no reason
items.why: The authoring entry points report a handled refusal as `{"error": …}` on stderr and print nothing on stdout. `console._forward` captured stdout only, so the payload was `{"output": ""}` and the tool could only render `create failed (exit 2).` — the actual error was destroyed, which is what made the root cause hard to find.
items.evidence: `_forward` now captures stderr, prefers the message inside the entry point's own JSON line (`_error_from`), keeps the raw text as `stderr`, and returns it all beside the payload; `console.main` exits 2 with the reason at the top level when a forwarded call failed, so a console consumer finds it where every consumer looks. The tool's renderer prefers `result.error`, then `stderr`, then `output`. A test drives a stub entry point that writes its refusal to stderr and asserts the reason reaches both the `_forward` payload and the console's printed payload, with exit 2.

items.title: Authoring verbs were synchronous and capped at ten minutes, with no run id to watch or resume
items.why: A real creation spends most of ten minutes before it writes a line of code. The tool's console timeout was 10 minutes and the authoring run happened in-process, so a long run was killed mid-flight, reported a timeout as its result, and could not be watched or resumed. The tool's own `start` action documents the opposite posture for searches.
items.evidence: The console's default timeout is 45 minutes (the config ceiling stays 60), and the tool's descriptions say authoring runs for many minutes inside the call. `status` reads an authoring run's own `.refactory/spine-status.json` and `facts.json` and reports the nodes done, the nodes due, the error and the run's facts, with `state` mapped from the spine (`done` -> finished, `ready` -> running, `failed`/`refused` -> failed) and `finished` true when the spine says done; the tool renders that as a sentence, so `status --run .factory/create/<name>` answers "where is it" while the call is still in flight. The console's authoring verbs take `--workdir` and forward it. Resume is NOT implemented: watching is what this delivers, and the note says so. Verified on the real run: `status` reported the create run's node-by-node progress while it ran.

items.title: The research stage produced nothing, and nothing noticed
items.why: `research-plan.json`'s only contract was `writes=("research-plan.json",)`, which any bytes satisfy. Two independent runs wrote a prose status message about subagents "running in the background" and left `research/` empty, and the design proceeded on unverified assumptions. The reason the subagents wrote nothing is the real defect: a node's model call runs on the one-shot profile, whose spawn subagent tool defaults to `backgroundMode: continuable`, so the agent ended its turn with its researchers still running.
items.evidence: Two changes, both required. (1) `DshModelClient` runs the one-shot profile with a checked-in overlay (`refactory_dsh/patches/agent-node.yml`) that patches the spawn subagent row to `backgroundMode: one-shot` and `enableRunInBackground: false` — the decision the graph profile already made for the CEO. (2) `record_findings` writes each direction's finding to `research/<slug>.md` when no subagent left one, and `gate_research` requires a JSON array of `{focus, slug, finding}` (three to five, non-empty, unique slugs) whose files exist, relooping with the reasons in `research-review.txt` and the `research_review` fact the node's prompt now reads; the design pipeline carries the same pair. Verified on a real run: before the overlay, two attempts produced the prose status message with `research/` empty and the gate caught both (research-review.txt named the file's first 200 characters); after the overlay the same prompt produced five findings files and a valid plan, and the gate wrote `ok`.

items.title: All create runs shared one fixed workdir, so concurrent runs collided
items.why: `--workdir` defaulted to the fixed `.factory/create`, so a second creation wrote its brief, research and strategy over the first one's, and a cancelled run's leftovers were what the next run read. Nothing distinguished two packages' state, and the console's create forwarder never passed a workdir at all.
items.evidence: The three authoring entry points default to `.factory/create/<name>`, `.factory/design/<name>` and `.factory/edit/<name>`; the console's create/edit/design verbs take `--workdir` and forward it when a caller gives one. Tests assert two names get two directories and that the default path ends in (`create`, `<name>`), and that the console forwards `--workdir` for all three verbs. The real run this session wrote to `.factory/create/buildroot_pack` and left its own research, strategy and staging there.

items.title: materialise nested a project-relative path under the package root, and validate reported a misleading missing manifest
items.why: The emit prompt asked for a `===FILE: <relative path>===` and never said relative to what, so the model wrote `refactory/refactory_packages/<name>/__init__.py`. Joined onto the package root that nested the package inside itself; the `is_relative_to` guard passed because the nested path really is inside the root; and `validate` reported `__init__.py is missing` four directories away, with a retry prompt that said nothing about paths, so every attempt repeated it.
items.evidence: The emit prompt states the convention (`__init__.py` means exactly `__init__.py`, not `<name>/__init__.py`, not `refactory/refactory_packages/<name>/__init__.py`, not `.factory/packages/<name>/__init__.py`). `_package_relative` strips a leading prefix that merely restates the package root, keeps a legitimate subdirectory, and refuses an absolute or `..` path by name. `sandbox.missing_init` names the root it looked in, what that root holds, and the convention, so the retry is actionable. Tests cover four prefixes, a subdirectory, the two refusals, and the message.

items.title: A node's model call ran in the checkout, so an agent's artifacts landed in the repository
items.why: The reviewing nodes are completions that spawn an agent with tools, and `DshModelClient` ran every completion with the checkout as its working directory. Relative paths the agent wrote therefore landed in the repository: the real create run left `reviews/code-review.md`, `reviews/health-check.md`, `reviews/qa.md`, `reviews/overwatch.md` and `reviews/overwatch-evidence/` at the checkout root while the run's own `reviews/` stayed empty. `synthesize_qa` reads the run directory, so it merged zero reviews, and the overwatch gate sent the build back to `emit` — a fifteen-minute reloop that looked like a model-quality problem. Found by the real run that proved the other five fixes.
items.evidence: `DshModelClient.complete` takes the directory to run in and spawns the completion there; the walker passes the node's run directory (`_ask_model`, which asks a client without the argument plainly because the vendored `ModelClient` protocol is still text in, text out); a caller with no run directory gets the scratch directory rather than the checkout, and the launcher path is absolute now that the child's cwd is not the repository. Tests: the client records the run directory it was told to use and the artifact lands there; a minimal client without the argument still works; a full create run's completions all run in the run directory and its reviews are there rather than in the checkout. The stray `reviews/` the real run left is deleted, and the workspace-hygiene test is what keeps a regression visible.

items.title: The tool could optimize a mode but not use it once
items.why: The tool's only execute action was `start`, the optimizer. `refactory run` existed as a CLI verb with no console verb, and the tool forwards to the console, so from the GUI a person who had just created a mode could not run it once and see its result.
items.evidence: The console gained a `run` verb forwarding to the interactive entry point (`--intent`, `--knob`, `--verdict`, `--workdir`, `--timeout`, `--provider`, `--model`), and the tool gained a `run` action named like the CLI's rather than like `start`. Because the one-shot runner prints its report from the child process — the terminal's stdout, not the console's buffer — the console reads the run directory back (`status` plus `facts.json`) and the tool reports where the run is, how it ended and what it recorded. Verified by running the real verb: `python -m refactory_dsh.console run counting_pack/fixed_step --intent "count to five from the GUI path"` completed all four nodes and returned exit 0. Tests: the console forwards every argument to `interactive`, a run without a mode is a usage error, the tool forwards the mode/intent/verdict/model, and the render names the run directory and the recorded facts.

items.title: A mode could ignore the brief's central input and still pass validate
items.why: `validate` proved a package was structurally a mode, not that it did what was asked. A brief whose entire subject was a Python package produced a mode that took no package at all — it built a fixture hardcoded in `ops.py` — and passed every check, because the pipeline had no representation of "the brief says this mode consumes X".
items.evidence: The inputs a brief declares are now first-class: `requires_input` is a knob (`--input NAME` on `python -m refactory_dsh.create`, `--input` on the console's create, `inputs` on the tool's create action, `--knob requires_input=…` from `ceo`); `declared_inputs` refuses a name too short to check; `prepare` publishes the list as a fact, and the design and emit prompts carry it, so the requirement reaches the code and not only the gate; and `validate` passes it to `sandbox.verify_sandboxed`, which refuses a produced mode with no declared knob named after the input and no read under that name, with a reason that says both ways to satisfy it. Tests cover the refusal, the pass (a knob named after the input), the too-short name, the prompts, and the console/tool forwarding. LIMIT, stated rather than implied: `validate` cannot read English, so a brief that never declares its inputs is unchecked — whether the work satisfies the brief stays a review judgement (the strategy review refuses a design that drops an ask, and the reviews read the brief). The issue's other suggestion — a reference artifact built independently of the mode's own writer — is a design change, not a fix, and is not implemented.

items.title: One transport blip discarded a whole authoring run
items.why: A 35-minute edit run died at `code_reviewer` on `dsh: TRANSPORT: DeepSeek API request ... failed` and everything already finished — research, strategy, design, emit, a passing validation — was unrecoverable: `DshModelClient` did one `subprocess.run` and raised on any non-zero exit, the graph's retry edges are domain-level gate reloops, and nothing could resume from the run directory. The error message also buried the cause under the model's trailing prose, so a transport failure read like a code-review defect.
items.evidence: Three changes. (1) `DshModelClient` retries a completion that failed on the wire (`is_transport_failure`: `TRANSPORT:`, socket-level spellings, rate limits, 5xx) up to three times with exponential backoff, and raises immediately for anything a model, a key or a prompt caused, so retrying cannot spend three completions on the same answer. (2) `failure_cause` reports the cause line rather than the last 500 characters of the model's reasoning. (3) The executor records how far it got in `.refactory/progress.json` — the next node after each success, the failing node with its error — and `Mode.resume` continues there with the recorded facts, knobs and task; `--resume <run dir>` is on `create`/`edit`/`design`, the console's three authoring verbs and the tool's three actions. Tests: the failing node is recorded with its error and the predecessor's facts; a resumed run continues at the failed node and does not rewrite an artifact that already existed (`number.json` doctored to 99 stays 99); a directory with no record is refused by name; transport-vs-content classification and the cause line. LIMIT: resume covers the in-process walker (the path the panel takes). A run driven by the DSH graph profile still has no resume plumbed through `interactive`.

items.title: validate and smoke exercised only the default knob path
items.why: A revision whose new input path emitted a `.dist-info` holding only `RECORD` — not a wheel — scored 1.0 on the built-in fixture and was accepted, because neither validate nor smoke ever supplied the input the brief asked for, and nothing looked at what the run produced.
items.evidence: `--sample NAME=VALUE` (repeatable; `sample` on the tool; a JSON array in the `sample_knobs` knob so a path with `=`, a comma or a space survives) supplies real knob values to the smoke, so the run exercises the input path rather than the declared defaults, and the message on failure names the samples it ran with. Independently, `artifact_problems` judges whatever the run produced by its own format: a `.whl` must contain `METADATA` and `WHEEL` beside its `RECORD`, and an unreadable `.zip`/`.whl` is refused by name — which is the check that would have caught the reported defect. `sandbox.smoke` gained the `knobs` override it needed. Tests: a wheel missing METADATA/WHEEL is refused with both named, a valid wheel passes, a non-archive is refused, a sample reaches the smoke's knobs, and a malformed sample is a usage error. LIMIT: a brief that declares no inputs, and a caller who gives no sample, still exercise only the default path; the format check covers archives, not arbitrary artifact kinds.

items.title: A bolded BLOCKING finding was invisible to the QA gate
items.why: Found by the hard sanity create run for a security-patch mode: its overwatch pass refused to state PASS and named the counter. `synthesize_qa` and `gate_qa` looked for lines that `startswith("BLOCKING")`, so a reviewer that bolded its marker was not counted — the synthesis said `0 blocking finding(s)` and the gate said `proceed` while the same body carried four blockers.
items.evidence: `marks(line, marker)` strips the decoration a markdown finding carries (bullets, emphasis, quotes, headings, leading whitespace) before comparing, case-insensitively; `synthesize_qa`, `gate_qa` and the overwatch verdict all use it. The test drives the synthesis over four spellings of the marker (`BLOCKING:`, `**BLOCKING:**`, `- **BLOCKING**`, `* BLOCKING:`) and asserts each counts as one blocking finding, that the header says so, and that the gate returns reloop.

items.title: A mode that raised inside the smoke was recorded as a measured 0.0
items.why: Same run, same overwatch pass. `sandbox.smoke` returns ok when the sandbox process exits 0, which it does even when the mode raises inside it, so `create_ops.smoke` read the payload's 0.0 score and recorded a measured score — reporting "it works badly" where the truth was "it does not run". The keyless path already distinguished not-measured from scored-nothing; the model and deterministic paths did not.
items.evidence: Both paths now check the payload's `exit_ok` and raise, naming the run's own error: the model path before accepting a score, the deterministic path after the model retry (so the keyless first attempt of an agent mode, which legitimately fails without a model, still reaches the retry). Test: a stub smoke returning `exit_ok: False` with a 0.0 score is refused with `did not finish a run with a model`.

items.title: A mode with frozen input knobs could not be run or searched
items.why: Found by using the mode the hard sanity create run produced. `refactory run … --knob source_root=…` failed with `knob 'source_root' is frozen and cannot be moved` because a person's override went through the optimizer's editor; `--knob target=7` could not set a numeric knob at all because the editor takes typed values; `optimize` had no `--knob` to seed a search, so a mode with frozen inputs scored the same thing for every candidate; and the model client was built only for the `autoresearch` optimizer, so every candidate of an agent mode failed with `agent node 'propose' needs a model client`.
items.evidence: `nn.edits.configure(state, name, value)` sets a knob for the run being made: it refuses an unknown name and a value the knob will not accept, and does not apply the freeze, because the caller deciding what this run operates on is not the search. `_from_text` parses a command line's text by the knob's kind (int/float/bool/numeric enum), so `--knob target=7` is the integer 7 and `--knob allow_regression=1` is True. `LoopConfig.knobs` seeds the starting state (the loop's own mode and the seed candidate), carried by `optimize --knob`, the console's `start --knob` (whose `_spawn` now emits one flag per list element) and the tool's `start` `knobs`. `loop.main` builds the model client unconditionally (fbfcf393e6), because the evaluator needs one for the mode's own agent nodes. Verified end to end: a real run of `cve_patch_pack/patch` with its two inputs scored 1.0, and `optimize` with those inputs evaluated candidates for real and recorded `set_knob attempts=2` as a scored 0.0 plus six validator refusals naming why each structural proposal did not fit. Tests: a frozen knob is settable by the caller, text is parsed by kind, a bad text is refused, the search's seed and the loop's own mode carry the seeded value, the console forwards `--knob` (not `--knobs`), the tool forwards one flag per value, and a search builds a client.

items.title: A review refusal relooped the build without telling it why
items.why: Found by watching the hard sanity create run: its overwatch pass refused twice (correctly — the produced mode could be scored 1.0 by deleting the failing test) and each refusal sent the graph back to `emit`, which re-emitted essentially the same design because `gate_qa` and `gate_overwatch` published no fact the emit prompt reads. Two full review rounds, about an hour, on the same findings. `review_design` (via `design_review`) and `validate` (via `validation`) already fed theirs back.
items.evidence: `gate_qa` publishes `qa_gate` (the blocking lines, quoted), `gate_overwatch` publishes `overwatch_review` (the reason plus an excerpt of what the audit found), both nodes declare the fact in `produces` in the create and design graphs, and both emit prompts interpolate them under "What the reviews refused". Test: the emit prompt names both facts, both gate nodes declare them, and driving the gates over a synthesis with a bolded blocker and an overwatch FAIL sets facts quoting the findings.

items.title: create asks for a class of work, and the data node is the harness's input port
items.why: A mode is a harness for a class of work, and create produced a single-shot by default: a harness could be tuned until one hardcoded example passed and shipped as if it generalised. Separately, Task.prompt() was declared, documented and implemented and read by nothing.
items.evidence: task_ref now implies the data node (data_node or bool(task_ref)); neither --task nor --single is refused before any model call -- verified by running it: `refactory ceo "count to ten" --mode create` exits 2 in 0.165s printing CREATION_DIRECTIVE, and `console create --name x --brief y` returns exit_code 2 with the same text. check_package refuses a package that bakes items in (inline_items, named file:line) or whose data node names neither a task_ref nor a source_path+source_format. Task.prompt removed from the protocol, the two shipped Tasks and the tutorial's hook table. 819 passed, 10 skipped.

items.title: The loop is graded on the train part of a Task's items and audited on the held-out part
items.why: Every candidate was scored on the items it was tuned on and nothing charged for size, so a search could win by memorising the items or by growing the graph.
items.evidence: Ran it end to end: `refactory optimize dataset_probe/dataset --holdout 0.5 --optimizer random --epochs 1 --batch-size 2` reported seed_score 0.97 against raw_best_score 1.0 (3 nodes x 0.01 parsimony), and the audit {train: 1.0, holdout: 0.5, gap: 0.5, overfit: true, threshold: 0.15, instances {train 1, holdout 1}} landed in holdout.json and in the report. `refactory adopt --run /tmp/rf-holo --as probe_adopted` then refused with exit 2 and the gap named; --allow-overfit is the override. The part travels as subset.json in the run directory, never as a mode knob.

items.title: The console reads the one-shot run the runner actually made
items.why: console.py read <project>/interactive/<mode> while interactive.py writes .factory/interactive/<mode>, so without --workdir the payload carried no run and the panel was told the console left no run directory while the evidence sat one path away.
items.evidence: interactive.default_workdir() is the one owner of the default and the console uses it. Running `python -m refactory_dsh.console run counting_pack/fixed_step` with no --workdir now returns a payload carrying run.status and run.facts. The new test fails with KeyError: 'run' against the pre-fix console line and passes after it (both runs recorded).

items.title: java_build_pack: the shipped example of a harness for a class of work
items.why: Every shipped package was deterministic or single-instance, so the product's canonical claim had no working example and the held-out audit had nothing with enough items to be meaningful.
items.evidence: A real model run of `refactory run java_build_pack/build --intent ... --workdir /tmp/rf-java-run` finished with final best score 1.0 and facts.json recording item_scores args 1.0, flat 1.0, nested 1.0 -- three Java trees, one build.sh written per item by the agent node, each judged by running the script and comparing the program's output. `refactory package verify java_build_pack` returns [] and the mode appears in `refactory list`.

items.title: The panel supplies a mode's knobs and can use a mode once
items.why: The panel could only press Start, which is the optimizer. A produced mode's inputs are its knobs, so every candidate ran inputs-empty and scored 0.0; and there was no way to use a mode once at all.
items.evidence: One field per declared knob, shaped by kind, all travelling as NAME=VALUE; a new @Remote run(...) reports the spine status, the nodes still due and the facts; Run once is offered exactly when the catalogue's own action is start. pnpm run test:gui: 340 files, 4762 passed, 1 skipped. pnpm run typecheck passed (regenerating the Typert face with run). verify-client-ui-i18n passed. Narrowed instrumented coverage put every touched file at 100%.

items.title: A run names the items a data node should read
items.why: A harness for a class of work is built once and fed many times; the only ways to feed it were to edit the mode or to invent an environment variable in its Task, and the panel could do neither.
items.evidence: Ran the shipped java harness against items it had never seen: `refactory run java_build_pack/build --source /tmp/rf-src-check --workdir /tmp/rf-src-run` wrote items.json {"*": {source_format: directory, source_path: /tmp/rf-src-check}}, iterated the one item there and scored it 1.0 (facts.json item_scores [{'id': 'one', 'passed': True, 'score': 1.0}]). 823 passed, 10 skipped.

items.title: A search may not bake its items in or rebind the Task it is graded on
items.why: create refuses a produced package that bakes items in and requires the Task that names the class of work; the edit algebra allowed both, so a candidate could memorise the items or choose its own exam.
items.evidence: Probed before the fix: set_node_field on inline_items, task_ref and source_path were all accepted by edits.apply. After it: inline_items raises EditError with code E-items from the shared finisher every primitive returns through, and Loop.step rejects a data node whose task_ref/source_path/source_format differ from the seed with E-exam. Both covered by new tests; 825 passed, 10 skipped.

items.title: The model smoke passes inside create and fails standalone, with an undiagnosable error
items.why: Two model-smoke paths disagree about a package that works, and the failure message is the tail of a Node crash banner rather than a cause, so the path was twice read as a failure of the whole creation.
items.deferred_reason: The pipeline's smoke of java_harness_v2 scored 1.0 as `sandboxed: true, model: used` while `refactory package smoke java_harness_v2/build --model` fails repeatably in 0.152s with `model completion failed (exit 1): Node.js v22.23.2`, and the sandbox's own stderr is empty. Which of the two passes the wrong thing to the client is not visible from outside the sandbox, and it is not blocking: create completes and the produced harness runs.

items.title: Own the IR, and make remote-factory a pinned test-only reference
items.why: Nine imported names cost 141 installed distributions, 459 MB of venv, 12 MB and 831 files in the repository. The reference is still worth keeping as the test-time oracle that catches our lowering bugs.
items.evidence: ir.py owns the IR (314 lines) with the reference's serialization reproduced byte for byte; no production module imports factory any more. Verified by running it: plain `uv sync` went from 142 installed distributions / 501 MB to 16 / 81 MB with `factory` absent; the suite without the oracle is 819 passed / 38 skipped and the toolchain gate reports the parity path unverified rather than passing silently; `uv sync --group reference` then makes tests/test_ir_parity.py pass 26/26, asserting byte-identity across all 22 shipped modes with the two documented REFERENCE_REFUSALS. Doc gates 15/15, recipes 15/15.

items.title: Depend on a pinned harness instead of copying it
items.why: We carry ~47 MB and 270 packages of upstream harness to run five packages of our own, and our entire delta on upstream code is one preset, a two-line web-app change, four generated files and two test expectations.
items.evidence: The copied harness (9,644 tracked files, 270 packages) is gone; the repository declares @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.1.5-rc.3 and keeps six packages. A clean clone was installed and run, not merely inspected: 264 tracked files; ./install.sh ran pnpm install --frozen-lockfile and pnpm run build to exit 0, uv sync installed 15 distributions, and dsh plugin --profile graph add created the profile under a fresh DSH_HOME; refactory doctor reported ready with 10 packages of modes. dsh_command() returned <clone>/node_modules/.bin/dsh, because apps/cli/src/bin.ts no longer exists. A real counting_pack/fixed_step through run_on_dsh exited 0 with .refactory/spine-status.json {"status": "done"} and facts.json {"value": 6, "steps": 3, "done": true, "final_count": 6, "steps_taken": 3, "closeness": 0.5}. The clone's pnpm run test passed 357 tests in 20 files. Install counts: one copy each of dsh-session, dsh-tools and dsh-shell, all 0.1.5-rc.3; 237 @deepseek-ai/dsh-* packages at 0.1.5-rc.3; one cordis@4.0.2. The three behavioural gaps the pin exposes (web picker rows, the console's generated Remote face, --provider/--model on the headless completion client) are issue #85.

items.title: Decide what our own verification becomes once the harness copy is gone
items.why: Removing the copied harness removes the doc gates, the snapshot suite and the bilingual pairing gate with it, so the replacement has to be chosen before the deletion rather than after.
items.evidence: refactory/docs/verification.md is the decision, written before the deletion and linked from contributing.md: the six packages' typecheck, build, vitest and lint; the glue's pytest suite with --run-integration as the end-to-end gate, the two generated-document --check commands and check_recipes; what replaced each deleted gate; what a contributor runs before pushing; and the three paths the surviving gates do not cover, now issue #85. The pairing gate's replacement is refactory/tests/test_docs_english_only.py, which fails on a .zh.md side or a README.i18n.yaml under refactory/ or the six packages; the three stale pairs under graph, workflow-spine and ui-brand-refactory are removed for it. Observed: the new test passes, the ledger's verify-path check passes after gui-42 stopped naming a deleted harness spec, and the clean clone's pnpm run test passed 357 tests in 20 files.

items.title: The web picker and the CEO preset work on the pinned harness
items.why: Deleting the copied harness removed the web composition that mounted the picker and the console, the generated Typert Remote face, the headless --provider/--model options, and the ceo preset. The mode path was unaffected, but the browser could not reach the picker and the outer loop's completion client ignored a named model.
items.evidence: Three pnpm patches in patches/, declared in pnpm-workspace.yaml, add what copying upstream used to: dsh-web-app gets rows for refactory-console, ui-refactory and ui-brand-refactory, disables ui-brand-official, defaults the agent preset to ceo, and declares our three packages so the loader resolves them; dsh-agent-presets ships the ceo preset directory; dsh-headless accepts --provider/--model and makes a named selection the middleware's current one. Verified in a clean clone, not only here: 267 tracked files, ./install.sh exit 0, the three patches applied (web-app mentions refactory in 3 manifest entries, agent-presets/presets/ceo holds both files, headless/lib/startup.js has --model), pnpm run test 357 passed. Against the clone's running pinned web app: the boot manifest lists refactory-console, ui-refactory and ui-brand-refactory; POST /api/refactoryConsole/modes returned {ok: true} with the real catalogue, which the gateway produces by runtime SRC discovery because the generated ./typert artifact does not exist; and /api/session/create with agentPreset ceo returned {ok: true, agentPreset: ceo} instead of the mount failure of issue #42. A real counting_pack/fixed_step through run_on_dsh exited 0 with spine-status done and facts value 6 / steps 3. The generated ./typert and ./remote artifacts are still not produced (the published generator needs its protocol as a workspace project); the gateway's SRC discovery and the hand-stated client face in src/types.ts cover the runtime, and the README and verification.md say so.

items.title: Drive a mode's graph from the chat and steer it mid-run
items.why: The web chat dispatched a run to a child process and polled it, so a person could not see the nodes or correct one. The spine also had no way to reopen a completed node or amend a node's prompt, and the ceo preset mounted no graph because a preset is composed once before any mode is chosen.
items.evidence: The spine gained redo(node) and amendPrompt(node, text, set|append) as wf_redo and wf_edit prompt actions, a wf_steer reader wired to the console (the single owner of the ledger format), and an interactiveOpen mode: wf_open lowers a mode through the console open verb, reads and validates the lowered graph, claims it for exec.agent.session, and refuses another session with 'a run is already open in another session'. Mounted in the ceo preset (patches/@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets) with inject [shell], so the spine's own guard denies the CEO's coding tools. One deterministic node per wf_next when interactiveOpen, and the graph profile's configured-graph path is unchanged. Verified: typecheck 0, pnpm run test 407 passed in 24 files, pytest refactory/tests 831 passed / 38 skipped, check_recipes 15/15, and a real counting_pack/fixed_step through run_on_dsh exited 0 with facts value 6 / steps 3. In a browser on the merged main: the CEO called wf_open then wf_next per node (4 mentions of wf_next in the page, 8 executions in the session record: start, step/check x3, finish), no bash call appeared, the run reached done with the mode's facts, a second wf_open refused with 'a run is already open in this session', no 'Failed to load plugins', no page errors (screenshots /tmp/issue89-drive.png and /tmp/verify-issue88.png). One in-session run per session is the accepted limit, stated in the README and verification.md.

verification.method: each item's recorded `verify` command was executed from the repo root
verification.note: two recorded paths were wrong and are corrected here: test_edit.py and test_design.py never existed (edit and design share test_edit_design.py). The loop-as-mode and lowering items now run with --run-integration, because their proof is a real DSH run.

closing_run.model_evidence: The run is model-backed, not a fallback: analysis/generation-0.md holds the proposer's own reasoning, and it cites a prior run's history (/tmp/strat-cli, best 1.04, order=asc) as grounds for the edits it made. That single artifact exercises the history access (#19), the gradient and guidance reaching the prompt (#26), and the reasoning optimizer behind the Optimizer seam (#20).
